issue.title: sase-core issue_type_migration_sql lacks the DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _issues_new restart guard
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-1sb.7 (epic sase-1sb, sqlite-robustness) note #1; triaged by sase-1sb.land on 2026-11-12.

`issue_type_migration_sql()` in the linked sase-core repo (`crates/sase_core/src/bead/schema.rs:92`, verified at sase-core 3416e4e2) starts with `CREATE TABLE _issues_new (` and has no `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _issues_new;` guard. Every later table-rebuild SQL in the same file (lines ~222, 318, 425, 547, 650) already has that guard. sase-1sb.7 fixed the same wedge in the Python copy (`src/sase/bead/_db_migrations.py::_migrate_issue_types`, commit b9572a8d59): if the rebuild dies after the CREATE, the leftover `_issues_new` makes every retry fail with "table _issues_new already exists" while `needs_issue_type_migration` still reports "not migrated".

Today the Rust function has no runtime caller. Only its own unit test (`issue_type_migration_preserves_and_accepts_claimed_status`) runs it, and the Python bead mirror uses its own inline SQL. It is still a public export from `sase_core::lib.rs`, so the first runtime caller would inherit a non-restartable migration.

Fix in sase-core: prepend `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _issues_new;` after `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF;`, and add a Rust test that pre-creates `_issues_new` next to an old-schema `issues` table and asserts `execute_batch(issue_type_migration_sql())` succeeds. Alternatively, delete the unused export if nothing should call it. No sase pin bump is needed unless a Python binding starts consuming it.

task_type_fields.impact: Latent: no runtime caller today, but any caller interrupted mid-rebuild leaves _issues_new behind and every later migration attempt fails, wedging the bead store until manual repair.
task_type_fields.repro: In sase-core: open an in-memory sqlite connection, create the legacy `issues` table (issue_type CHECK without 'plan'), run `CREATE TABLE _issues_new (id TEXT)`, then `conn.execute_batch(issue_type_migration_sql())`. It fails with "table _issues_new already exists". Read `crates/sase_core/src/bead/schema.rs` lines 92-125: no DROP guard, unlike lines ~222/318/425/547/650.

issue.creation_reason: sase-1sb.7 made the Python issue-type rebuild restartable, but the exported Rust copy of the same migration SQL still lacks the DROP guard. That leaves a latent wedge for any future caller.

payload.description: sase-1sb.7 fixed the same restart wedge in the Python copy (src/sase/bead/_db_migrations.py, commit b9572a8d59); mirror its DROP guard and test
